title: Strict tensor comparison for finite coefficient-reduction towers
statement: For the completed coefficient sheaf R on X_proet and its finite quotients S_n, the strict tower obtained by reducing the ordinary direct-sum total tensor of any two R-complexes is naturally isomorphic to the strict tower of the total tensors of their two separately reduced complexes. Both towers are read as R-module complexes by the recorded scalar restrictions. No boundedness or K-flatness is required. The finite reduction and transition functors are those of def-weil-integral-reduction-tower and lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined; the total tensor is def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model.

source.place: Section tensor products (section-tensor-product), scalar-extension identity immediately following the sectionwise tensor construction; sheafification compatibility in lemma-sheafification-tensor. Combined with total complexes, Stacks 06YM and 07A4; Bhatt--Scholze Definition 3.4.10.

proof.text: Use the ordinary scalar-extension tensor isomorphism, normalized by the adjunction unit on pure sections. Apply the total-complex tensor comparison and its naturality to obtain a finite-level natural isomorphism. Its generator equation is obtained by evaluating on the total-summand injections and the scalar-extension unit.

For every consecutive pair of quotients, apply the normalized transition-compatibility lemma. Form a natural transformation of the two strict towers with NatTrans.ofOpSequence. Its components are the finite-level isomorphisms, so it is an isomorphism; their naturality makes this natural in both input complexes.

proof_origin.note: Extract the strict finite-level comparison and the separate quotient-compatibility argument from the completed tensor calculation; no derived descent is included in these lemmas.
